Bachelor's degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training
Experience coordinating HR activities, purchasing/reimbursements, finance and/or operations.
Experience working in a research environment.

Experience using generative AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Copilot) and automation or no-code tools to streamline administrative or operational work, including building reusable AI-assisted workflows (e.g. custom assistants, templates or automations) rather than only ad hoc use, with sound judgment about data privacy and security.
Experience coordinating HR activities, purchasing/reimbursements, finance and/or operations within higher education institution(s).
Demonstrated experience designing, documenting and implementing new processes, workflows or standard operating procedures (not only following existing ones), and improving them over time.
Experience supporting grant proposals or research administration (e.g. preparing budgets, budget justifications, biosketches or sponsor reports).
Experience in a small or fast-growing organization (e.g. a start-up, non-profit or new research group) where operational processes had to be built from scratch.

The Lab Coordinator runs the operational side of the Pandemic & Epidemic Threat Analysis Lab (PETAL), a computational research group of about ten people in the School of Public Health working to reduce the risk from pandemics and other major biological threats. The Lab Coordinator owns lab operations and logistics, HR and appointments, financial management, purchasing and reimbursements, and research administration end to end, enabling PETAL's researchers to spend their time on research that improves how the world prepares for and responds to outbreaks.

The Lab Coordinator is a core member of the team. Alongside running the lab’s day-to-day operations, this position builds the systems, standard operating procedures and AI-enabled workflows that keep those operations efficient as PETAL expands. The role is motivated by PETAL’s public-health mission, takes ownership, and spots and fixes problems before they land rather than waiting to be asked. As the lab grows, there is substantial scope for the role to grow with it, including taking on wider responsibility, contributing to grant development, managing relationships with funders and partners, and shaping how the lab plans and runs its operations.
Track record of taking ownership of work: spotting problems or inefficiencies early and resolving them with minimal direction.
Interest in public health, pandemic preparedness or biosecurity, and motivation to contribute to PETAL’s mission as a core member of the team.
Proficient in communicating clearly and effectively, both verbally and in writing, and in integrating information in the completion of assignments.

Proven ability to organize work functions in an efficient and effective manner.
Thorough knowledge of common computer applications and web-based collaboration tools; ability to learn new technological platforms.
Strong customer service orientation, including excellent interpersonal skills to be able to work with a wide range of faculty, researchers, staff, and students.
Ability to use sound judgment in responding to issues and concerns.
Ability in problem identification and reasoning; ability to develop original ideas to solve problems.
Ability to work effectively both independently and in collaboration with team members.
Thorough knowledge of common computer applications and web-based collaboration tools; ability to learn new technological platforms.
